说起来O哥也已经有十几年的驾龄了（好像有十三四年了？），如果按驾龄算，那大概也算得上是老司机啦。


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRtCud2TB4BSp7BEW278RwGsYEwpsv3neA7tuzWMAY8Dx/image.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

其实O哥是个很懒的人，一直懒得考驾照，哪怕后来有娃了，为了方便出行买车了，我还是懒得学，合计家里有媳妇这个司机就可以啦。

后来发生了一些事情，不得不学开车，不得不去考驾照，就这样，O哥被赶鸭子上架，成了一名驾驶员。

O哥成为驾驶员之后，也是很抵触开车的，毕竟啊，开车多累人。我记得有一年开车去大连玩，几天内大概开了2000左右公里，回来累得好多天都直不起来腰呢。

所以无论去哪里，能不开车的情况下，我绝不开车，一般都会选择公共交通出行（公交、地铁、高铁、共享单车），实在着急的时候，就叫网约车。

就算是回老家，除非是全家人一起回，大包小裹拿很多东西的情况下，我选择开车，若是自己一个人往返，我都选择高铁。

其实乘坐高铁回老家无论是时间上还是花销上一点也不省啊，金钱就不说了，时间上打车到高铁站，高铁站等车，高铁运行，打车回家，没个三四个小时到不了，而我开车，最快一个半小时就可以到呢。

但是高铁我省事呀，好吧，其实是我懒。

所以，开车近十年，我才开了几千公里（出去玩几趟+回老家），被朋友们嘲笑得不得了，说我家的车就是浪费，哈哈。


![b5f4934ee0feef45f20e287723e21836.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTCTsfyHv5y1PafDCHByAP39R5BSQ4L47t2tk3fkBwUf9/b5f4934ee0feef45f20e287723e21836.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)


什么时候开车变得多了起来呢？大概是从儿子读初中开始吧，他上小学时学校就在家门口，步行上学就可以。但是初中离家三四公里，总不能还步行呀。

于是“老司机”开始开始接送娃的日子，我还记得第一天送娃，我被俩排车挤到马路中间骑线前行，然后被旁边的大客车刮了我的后视镜，卡卡卡都刮掉漆了。

儿子气够呛，让我追上大客车，让它赔钱，可是我心虚得不得了，我没开在正常的车道里，人家不找我赔钱就不错啦。

反正开始天天开车送娃的那段时间，真的是状况频发，好在事情都不大，最严重的一次是想变道插队，被后边专业碰瓷的车顶了上来，基本上双方车辆都没啥大损害，但被人家讹了300大洋，每次想起这事我都意难平呀。

就这样接送了初中三年，我从“驾龄”上的老司机，变成驾驶经验上的老司机，慢慢地也开始飙车啦。

尤其是儿子上了高中以后，路程翻倍，上学放学时间又紧，超级考验车技，现在每趟行程，我都要比高德预估的快好多。

原本我还为我的车技以及飙车速度沾沾自喜，结果这几天大家在群里聊接送孩子的话题，发现真的老多飙车大神的啦。

比如我早晨送娃六公里，最快的时候也要十一二分钟，结果人家20公里，也才15分钟，没法比呀没法比。


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRH72NM8er6igGKZw9W4y8Q8qaw4jhJ4do3se4hAxmfka/image.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

看到这些信息后，我突然发现，自己有时候也太在意和追求速度了，这样其实是不对的，安全才是第一位呢。

所以我决定以后接送娃不能飙车了，虽然不能慢慢开，但也要稳稳开。毕竟我飙车使大劲就能省出三两分钟，而儿子每次回家闲聊都能聊上半个多小时（甚至更多），这三两分钟，哪里省不出来呢？

*Zhinvali is a scenic townlet and major artificial reservoir located on the Aragvi River in the Dusheti Municipality of the Mtskheta-Mtianeti region in Georgia*
*Zhinvali (also Jinvali; Georgian: ჟინვალი) is a townlet in Georgia, Dusheti Municipality (Mtskheta-Mtianeti region), on river Aragvi. It has one of the largest hydroelectric power stations in Georgia.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhinvali*

![20251209_110017(2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/23s9MKcdiAbA2PDjcL2Dcv3ETXkRHjcWESHHyXFZEfyeWdhHr2qfYZ2be23XDSPCkFNy2.jpg)

![20251209_110017(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/245Hej1NHqhHpTzsprqYiZ8GSuRUVfdXmZHYtHvEvmTyAStcBNez59nBEAXKbhZN4kYTT.jpg)

The third day of our tour took us quite far from Tbilisi, as our tour guide told us that it would take an hour or more to reach our destination. He picked us up at our hotel at seven in the morning. My husband and I were both excited to explore the eastern part of Georgia and discover more of its beautiful landscapes. Since it was still early, I felt sleepy during our journey and decided to take a nap in the car. Before closing my eyes, I asked my husband to wake me up when we were getting close to our destination. My husband gently woke me up, and I immediately looked outside the window. I was surprised by the beautiful scenery surrounding us. Our tour guide told us that we were just a minute away from our destination so I quickly took out my phone to capture some pictures along the way. The view was already incredible with enormous mountains rising into the sky and turquoise water stretching along their base. Some of the mountain peaks were covered in snow making the landscape look even more beautiful. We also passed a massive heart-shaped archway that framed the majestic mountains perfectly. I felt excited because I knew we were about to see something truly special.

![20251209_110331.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EnYPWxyi8MXJcvEoHQ2u6fi25bZj1QmqSf1mPQ9dFKNNrYKPw8ugQodYBR3UFU1hU2J.jpg)

![20251209_110334.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EqQKdQNcuCcaCC3NdGtpSjD2aN8Jxz4QNudd8TcFYbmWamEaDyvGfpJKvFnAo86rpZ3.jpg)

When we stepped out of the car, my husband and I went straight to the viewing deck. The moment I saw the breathtaking view in front of me, I was completely stunned. The turquoise waters of Zhinvali Reservoir looked incredibly beautiful. It was surrounded by impressive mountain crests. The tour guide told us that Zhinvali Reservoir is an artificial lake, a hydroelectric reservoir on the Aragvi River that helps supply water to Tbilisi. Learning a little about the place made our visit even more riveting. We understood that this gorgeous stop also plays an important role in the daily lives of the people.

![20251209_110716.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EqUctRS7oPdhTq7wdg13aEuTsLVMMo9H6fusbb4y5S6VvhKHDRhdwvigowd49Vt5GnP.jpg)

![20251209_110722.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EnugszZn2DKzAKaTEQiECyecxtw6WAqA6FNqYJJNfYsk1QP5PrjSpgwbpnyqS7iT1Rh.jpg)

![20251209_111311.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EnWFdV9J1XfGDLXbQRRNnmuUmpAGfE7YpeZsWzkaNVaqaa8wJMhtyeVMGVAesgWMxd5.jpg)

![20251209_111320.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EqUcvVm3HJPwvBU3AGrWWnx4qHm9E4hZHp3LfMSicqWFANg7Mnze1C513ruTCrvMHKH.jpg)

![20251209_111604.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EnYPyX5RoJS1ibotGaJhgV7Lf6pPoRbrwcyUcGvSNrkahNWCYUHEfePUWmjbX3c79e2.jpg)

I could hardly resist taking photos of the surroundings. I was completely starstruck by the beauty of nature. Everything looked like a painting. The water was placid and smooth. The striking mountains rose sharply from the water's edge with their slopes covered in thick vegetation and bushes. Taller and more jagged mountains displayed patches of snow while some of the highest peaks were gorgeously snow capped. The mixture of turquoise water, mountains and snowy peaks created a stunning contrast.

![20251209_111116.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EoPM7TRDgfoGvKCZXxHnsVwB8MCHcUujLoiaygAfki5NjYeGuCTf5Muk5dZF6MeM2gC.jpg)

![20251209_110634.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EnWG36p9V7mDU51X915XwpPEps9Rc8QxZ29wWjBwLMwPD66opsnic2gxbX8cTvQ5R8H.jpg)

![20251209_111124.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gretelarmfeg/EqBan2Q4yXH6AauLQcPztypJYdW4EJRW2jWYwnR5Ywm36Q1Hd8KPBjcxBixw5St3Jbo.jpg)

My husband and I felt incredibly happy to witness such a wonderful creation of nature. I was filled with admiration and gratitude. Although it was time to continue our journey a part of me wished we could stay a little longer. Zhinvali Reservoir truly captured my heart and leaving was not easy when the scenery was so mesmerizing.

So... I am in Tbilisi... Leaved Kolkata for Mumbai and had a flight to Georgia 5 weeks ago. Loved that month in Georgia - it's much-much quiter here and everything is more predictable than in crazy (amazing) India 😄 And old Tbilisi's alleys are full of textures and kitties ❤️ - sharing images from a very recent walk. 😎

![DSC_0332.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/242Y9vR22FyMR4GmdoofVdcoFWNkBg8uwbDPTktPgZ52gJAYivYjpjtCo95w7vMXpukfy.JPG)

That's the style - 2-storey buildings with wooden balkonies are a signiture architecture of the old town.

![DSC_0340.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/243M9A7dwDh3Z2Xtc29ZmK3wHnUfwh72ztd7FehgykYD8WvkTj92PpUoQNMzWNLuhmAuC.JPG)

A significantly gentrifided area, but still with the charm.

I sort of tired of street photography lately and love to focus on the cats especially 'cause I have a cat community on Reddit, if you don't know - reached 5K members recently 😊🥂

![DSC_0327.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23uQjuuGAGTwyMMusKUWntzX8FdbZyxooYe9NPV1nn5WUTrfk44iEQaPwKT6WAvY9X3Rn.JPG)

![DSC_0328-3.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23zbWR6hV3J6BQ33Bz3LAfa8rwTt6Ky8qHe5ZJhsR6ScBSJvqwdCce6dRUpD5DYdzTbVu.JPG)

More cats on the way.

![DSC_0357.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23u67LGmz3LrU5pfccCfzzanekKBbbadMhjMuSYdRFHnmDefY7RnzM2VK7jch7aa1HPfd.JPG)

Although social media prefers vertical shots, I search for opprtunities of combining people and street life with cats:

![DSC_0368.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23u5vfLDFhLb98LQXMGhPLnUBqJMnXrjs8Tx5h2twTCFnYyRUckAzW1y6KHNLbATviMKU.JPG)

![DSC_0374.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23wqcBgCBupbrDmH4VUrbPotPMRW7DNEXnMPpsyPPrfo2by9fJq9DrwjHK4ZdGP5EfVzY.JPG)

![DSC_0378.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23tkpRw1cQkyBfrdd96H65xc1hWdL96MhFEGDvZtH1cscd9WxAyLp7f9qhimBCNgME2H9.JPG)

![DSC_0383.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23uFKXpfdtHMT22KmF1fv3Au4Zcjyy21uGeNTH8vpmCdKHTsz4DjCuhQgbc9fzJvVuCYM.JPG)

![DSC_0386.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23w2cMn5AZa3GUBS5Wi6jpbh2Zt4HkzLj89puxdiC6AodTNoqT7AAUpAFk8Yf88vRsEjp.JPG)

It's like the second summer here, +25 in the afternoon, +18 in the evening - perfect for long walks.

![DSC_0390.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23wgHHifbr7fKwHSrxdZ9uphqm7rhFEdPtwB6Kvu2utz2wPjXAjfFWmLo8rDHML2mgDro.JPG)

Cats, even stray, feel good in old Tbilisi - supported by people, locals, expats, and travelers.

![DSC_0395.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23tbRPyssUKyP1ozqzGRP5qYnt57nVE7pVz2cBEg2jv1BS3KrfsiJcTa6XZkiFqtvdwSc.JPG)

A beautiful city, Tbilisi is. I have several walks a week, each 15-20 km long. So, more shots of cats and streets are ahead, stay tuned, dear reader! 😎

As for Mumbai and Kolkata - a lot of cool images I took there, I'll share them later as soon as I start feeling nostalie for that part of my life journey... I will - guess I might return to India at some point - Mumbai, Goa, Kerala would be fantastic.

With summer knocking on the door, it is time for our 24-hour flowers to appear.
![095.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23wWvt2vZrHbwJ9iM29uM8rSrD8vM5PydysfBaCT1sgDPuhV5YshkTKcBF5bk1dF876wh.jpg)

Every year this time these magnificent flowers start to appear, and a few years ago we had twenty something flowers that appeared all at the same time, and it was a wonderful show.  

I think that the flower specie name is *Echinopsis werdermanannii*, and they originate in Paraguay. We have about 60 little plants all crowded in a narrow space alongside the outer wall of our back garden, and as soon that the sun shifts into such a position that the light lands on the plants, then they start to flower. The rest of the time they are in the shade. I suppose that one can start to uproot and untangle the plants in order to plant them separately, but I will have to find a cactii expert to come and do this. Each of the plants surround themselves with "babies", and I think they are starting to choke themselves.  

They bloom overnight as you can see in the picture below, and to me, that's when they are the most beautiful.
![092.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/48Qtwt261C1ySaQ12n4ozAbLY3JG65qPSwzicNobEqk57Zt7UasYk6GHVxWny9suSg.JPG)

Even at dawn, they look very nice.
![094.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EogNGqq4W41iUVKSuwEcLyCmhsEEDateq8BQ56e2CZh5HfGcwEmnFDAusYrTmzHgZ6B.JPG)

24 hours done, and the flower is kaput.
![045.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoK7MFn9sw9R6afY7qiseaXi3qE9xnVdBVbpCHiDjMDMWwsq8p9N5v7427swVuBAPxc.JPG)

But not to worry, as there are 5 new ones starting to grow on this plant. Also have a look how it surrounds itself with smaller ones.
![047.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EogPDYcD5p5WqyozLGXC4e9Bn4rsfZ7iaTMQLu6yjoHLb3uGm8umGiJUNRbo4mV99EH.JPG)

See the short grey brownish stems on the other plants, they are all flower stems, and we counted 8 thus far in total. I will be sure to share every bloom in my blog. 
![050.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Eou8dH7YzbKbKrEfynp5dfZsRcdWbEV9RfmWTg2JWYpS5bjhduB3a8ux4njgjyR9Ntd.JPG)

This small cactus is bravely sprouting its little flowers, and maybe it wants to compete with the 24-hour flowers. Lol
![049.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23uFYHFo6SXiJGyECotvbLkGbjeuWvaSqijCVJnTf3tkx17pnT5qXHFvkco653osAUyNx.JPG)

And finally, just a female Carpenter Bee on an Ornamental Spurflower (Plectranthus ornatus).
![007.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EogMNVzUxxdKzDpuj1D3rYDcnWfA3uYNWP4CyRNzz3Xr8A3DYSF97BBm1tpHHJU2Uz4.JPG)

We have a book title, Field Guide to Succulents in Southern Africa, and I forgot about it, so now the wife shoved the book under my nose. Lol. At last, I can put some put some names to flowers and I don't feel so useless anymore when it comes to flowers. Whenever I see some lovely flowers, then I simply cut a piece of stem, dunk it in hormone powder and then stick it into the ground. Sadly, that's not the way to do it, and that is why the flowers that I plant don't grown. 

I think everything in life has a special application, and carelessness nowadays is starting to turn everything upside down. Everyone seems to be in a great hurry. It is so essential to stop and smell the roses again. But there are very few that do that. Rushing about is never going to be a healthy practice, and it often results in illnesses. Our bodies are of the frailest on the planet, and they can only take so much as then things start to break down. But hey, who wants to rest when there is so much going on?
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story.

Photos and words by Zac Smith. No AI and no Photoshop. All-Rights-Reserved.

Camera: Canon PowershotSX70HS Bridge camera. 

Until next time. Shalom!

話說，九月是非常忙的一個月。我們家的老佛爺，我家小拉拉和我阿姨，她們三個都是九月生日的，也都是在中秋季節這段時間。所以，每逢到了中秋，你們拉叔我卡是需要慶祝好幾次的，

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS9UWffX74eEiP2BTxjb9LX48C8P5VSo6JRpDnu9h6LDR/1792481849370.jpg)
小拉拉去了補習班，我們三人到商場去買一些日用品。然後順路進去金加利吃個晚飯。我點了個公仔面吃，算是簡單的一餐。


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYszQ4sQPY2oUophpX3FgfTBeWBAT5aKqFcLqmSNKoH8e/1792481849469.jpg)
可是，單點個方便麵又好像不太夠。於是，找到其實套餐也不錯的。因為多加幾塊錢就可以多一條熱狗。這東西如果單點的話可是要整十塊錢呢。於是，我的套餐立馬又在升級，多追加了個絲襪奶茶。

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSKjoqT26ex7JdgjMxpGRbyzgoG6PsowMtBn9ojpg6PoM/1792481849555.jpg)
母老虎可沒上當，她不點套餐。她要的是肉碎炒茄子，鍋氣非常到位。她再另外單點個奶茶。我算了一下，其實這個算盤打得挺響的，價格的確跟我的套餐比起來便宜幾毛錢，不過這就少吃很多了。結果，一埋單，又是整百塊錢。這當然還包含我家大小姐點的白醬意大利面，沒有拍到照片我就不加註釋了。

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRVjEeGG6ZTbbsCczRDvbMU5T21xpuFNtZ2FVqpbZbUu4/1792481849649.jpg)

隔天我們到教堂去讓母老虎收拾和整理一哈她的詩歌。每逢週末我們都會到教堂去唱歌，而週日也會回去收拾詩歌，方便下個禮拜用。我們一般都會到教堂附近的印度店去吃早餐。我點了的是鳥巢飛餅。其實就是印度飛餅家兩個蛋嘛。

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWmqsGkGLcbHMJ94YQQotKfan9yQ2CqbEdRrVVsybNUUj/1792481849733.jpg)
收拾完詩歌，我們立馬就開車趕路回去老家找老媽了。回到家其實已經時間不早，於是我們又帶著老媽開車出去吃個客家餐廳。我是沒敢點什麼，只拿了個空碗。結果，大家的菜都不肯吃，於是我就點了一碟麵，什麼都沒，連調味都沒的，於是就替大家更下了他們不要的。

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmarYuFxPMexXix7xdbqYEzGZK1vVbhZ3u4foieEJ2wxYG/1792481912784.jpg)
小拉拉和大小姐各自點了咕嚕肉套餐，母老虎的是雞酒麵線，老媽的是豬腳醋。他們把1不喜歡的菜，都扔了過來給我。我的最新生存之道就是，我什麼都不點，就等著吃他們剩下的。一方面省錢，第二方面不浪費食物。

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYqhaZ8Y9JHaEofoJNVLHynifuCEBc8BW3Xj1SSsGczee/1792481912872.jpg)
當天晚上，我們和老媽吃了個晚飯，慶祝了生日後，我們馬上開車又趕路回吉隆坡，因為隔天是你們拉叔我回去找陳小姐牙醫師了。這次，也一樣沒有辦法為我治療。不知是我太緊張，還是所有菇涼恐懼症，每次到醫院量血壓的時候都爆表的。護士，我可以摸摸你的小心臟嗎？啊不，我是說你可以摸摸我的小心臟嗎？

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVaZ6zNmLdBuk8YGXZj5qbSPPnAkffQB7fUEc43xmE9oA/1792481912984.jpg)
雖然是請了假，不過早上見牙醫後，反正我也是閒著，於是就搭單軌回去公司，準備去顧客哪裡坐坐吃個午飯打打屁。這是才發現，我們的單軌官方終於肯把這風扇給洗一下了。現在大風了很多，也不會突然有一大片灰塵吹過來我頭頂了。

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNQutx2jqMkB7hZhHbfVu2EwQ8HA6VpUCgHky45XtDLsT/1792481913075.jpg)
我們顧客可是對拉叔不錯了，雖然我們給的福利不多，但是他們還是繼續支持著用我們的保險。可能是總經理跟我差不多年紀，大家還算聊得來，對於業績分配還是很賞臉我們的。

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWFSTFhuz4x8nzECRsLnpGZD449ZRoRvwmSfzM2Sy4MVS/1792481913134.jpg)
這回程時決定出來走走，省個地鐵站費用，還可以順便當散步運動。不走還好，已經過這裡，看到了原來hard rock在搞特點午餐套餐。買三個人分，送一個人。感覺超值啦。可惜，只做星期一到星期五。

I suppose this feeling that time is flying by is due to the number of complex events that have taken place in the streets of this town recently. And I'm not talking about things that involve scandals, squabbles, or notorious outbursts, no... The truth is, I'm talking about everyday life, which here is usually accompanied by a lot of situations that, for someone who doesn't live in Venezuela, would surely seem like something out of a dystopian novel by George Orwell... For example, today I got home at 5:30 PM after working in a nearby town, and here in my town we were without electricity and without any internet service, so I had to wait until 9:30 PM to "have a little bit of normalcy" and do some pending things at home, things which, of course, depended on these services... So, all this, repeated day after day, ends up affecting the psyche of those of us who have already been subjected to this multitude of complications for decades in a very complex way... And well, I don't like to harp on about the same thing, but it's difficult to detach oneself from or isolate oneself from the impact this causes... And yet, this catharsis of mine Being able to sit down at my PC whenever time allows is truly valuable, because photography has been my daily therapy for so long that I'm even struggling to find the words to describe what it does for me... But anyway, let's move on and please appreciate these street photos from last September, which, as I said before, already seems so long ago... >**S**eptiembre terminó hace menos de tres semanas, y sin embargo parecen haber pasado un montón de días desde entonces. Supongo que esta sensación de que el tiempo pasa rápido, se debe a la cantidad de eventos complejos que han sucedido en las calles de este pueblo recientemente. Y no hablo de cosas que impliquen algún escándalo, rifirrafes o alharacas notorias, no... La verdad es que hablo de lo cotidiano, lo cual aquí suele venir acompañado de un montón de situaciones que, para alguien que no viva Venezuela, seguramente parecerían sacadas de una novela distópica de esas que escribiría George Orwell... Por ejemplo, hoy a llegué a casa a las 5:30 PM después de trabajar en un pueblo cercano y aquí en el mío estábamos sin electricidad y sin ningún tipo de servicio de internet, entonces hube de esperar hasta las 09:30 PM para "tener un poquito de normalidad" y hacer algunas cosas pendientes en casa, cosas las cuales por supuesto, dependían de estos servicios... Entonces, todo esto repetido día a día termina por trastocar de manera muy compleja de la psiquis de nosotros quienes ya hemos estado sometidos este montón de complicaciones por décadas... # Sharing the Vahan Puja (worship of vehicles) with my son ![20261019_083607.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23uFTybHmJkX9gUJtLDJtcEtsB7B9bTr1eMGKMNYz8fFeUbQe4BoexZndJKEcxm4jK3Fa.jpg) **Dussehra** or **Vijayadashami** is a festival to celebrate the victory of good over evil and apart from celebration, there is a deeply personal, mandatory ritual in our household that truly anchors the spirit of this day - the beautiful tradition of Vahan Puja or worship of vehicles. In our culture, tools, machinery, and vehicles are never treated as mere inanimate, mechanical objects. They are revered as extensions of divine energy that help us sustain our livelihoods, keep our daily routines moving, and, most importantly, safely transport our families. This annual ritual is an expression of deep gratitude to these silent partners in our journeys, acknowledging the divine energy flowing through the instruments of our daily life. ![20261019_083203(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23w2kgmt3nBfCUPgKLgzMM6qQKJEfqa1EoJwSwJtHAhRSefci9D8jcQNdHAuTW1WU2Fc8.jpg) This year’s celebration held an even deeper meaning for me, as I took the opportunity to actively involve my son and pass down these foundational family rituals to him. It is one thing to watch a tradition, but an entirely different experience to participate in it, understanding the why behind every single action. The entire process turned into a wonderful family affair that required dedication and care, which involved cleaning of every single vehicle we own - from the cars down to the humble two-wheelers and even bicycles, nothing was left behind. To ease our burden a bit, we had actually taken the cars to the showroom for a professional service just three or four days prior. Yet, tradition is tradition, so we still sprinkled water over the wheels to symbolically purify them before the ritual began. The bicycles, however, were a completely different story. My son and I had to roll up our sleeves and scrub those down ourselves - after all, there is no authorized service showroom for a bicycle 😀 ![20261018_163126.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23wqieDAvt4j32CMVL7wRGB2zpct3895sdk37bjQv8CbvTXT2jgesVVPThzMYnGD7jkMb.jpg) Watching him participate in the ritual with pride made me realize that these manual moments are where values are truly inherited. Once all the vehicles were ready, we beautifully adorned the front panels with marigold flower garlands and ensured everything was kept perfectly ready. ![20261019_082608.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23uFRN55SMiKWnCa4uoMUstZUnkDLiQKFJ27XEjw7kAd8npRx16VBU7JkYexiDndwUoZb.jpg) ![20261019_083521.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23xeffCyaWtYUZGDFEwT1698HPH8ksgjpKy5EYNtYComksvqDFR47SqZEgs2RaUKcxLnJ.jpg) We then welcomed our temple priest, who came to officially perform the sacred rituals. I had my son stand close by to observe the precision of the ceremony. With experienced hands, the priest drew the Swastika - the ancient symbol of auspiciousness and protection - onto the vehicles and tied the sacred red fabric tied with bangles, to the steering wheels, adding a profound layer of sanctity to our efforts. ![20261019_084006.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23u63FBVCNZjbxK6VCx1NAVHFvLFwGxHhKWppDaBomkBe9v8116V9EKc9hpAj14CTc5r1.jpg) The culmination of the puja under the priest's guidance was filled with immense focus and reverence. He lit the camphor and incense sticks, chanting sacred mantras while performing the aarti around the vehicles to invoke Goddess Durga's blessings to remove obstacles and protect our future paths. ![20261019_084324.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23u6BQRgGBva1jjoFuryY9sMkm6cgzugrL89DL3S1gySsBDkLV1ZsaMrbDUciviAxfEtM.jpg) After the priest performed the rituals, we moved to the highly anticipated final step - placing four fresh lemons underneath the tires. Sitting behind the wheel, starting the ignition, and driving forward to crush the lemons served as our traditional shield to ward off negative energies. ![20261019_084836.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23u673L6yJiAQXajL9cApdjGyAaEns2KL7yQjX34Aeqb4aqCo2TnCVZvwBKZctJdbfQMb.jpg) Seeing my son witness the rituals made me incredibly proud to pass down a tradition that keeps our family grounded, safe, and protected for all the journeys in the year ahead. As a parent, it's absolutely necessary to teach them the value of our traditions, ensuring they carry these anchors of gratitude, humility, and culture with them as they navigate their own paths in life. ![hive.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sanjeevm/23t7Yf2ig7CziqatXGLDSFvEXbGWpLghnimWmyzQWE2BichH69ZtADrPf9j3fQTtbt3cw.png)

---------------------

It's not happening as quickly as I would like, but slowly my wife and I are filling in the map we have of the United States.  This year was actually pretty special for us as we got to add five of the little wooden pieces to the map that was given to us for Christmas a few years ago.  Sadly, there are still a lot of open spaces to fill, but I am confident that given time, we can change that. While I wouldn't put any one state above the others among the new five we visited together this year, Wisconsin is a little special mostly for the fact that we hauled our travel trailer there and camped this summer. 

I had been to Wisconsin a few times myself through the years, but as I mentioned, this was the first time we had visited the state together.  The rules of our map are that we can't add pieces if we haven't been there together, and we also can't add pieces if we are just in the state for a layover or something like that.  For example, a year or two ago when we went to Vermont, we had a connecting flight in Atlanta.  We never left the airport, so Georgia still remains unfilled on our map.

<center>![PXL_20260711_154450752.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/242NcpLibjKahq1qPKnFvF46dUfbX3qEQRwhuDQk2bBup3HttedVouDkvmte2qRZnqsvC.jpg)</center>

---------------------------

Wisconsin is a pretty cool state as far as states go.  I mean, cheese, beer, and bratwurst, what can you really hate about that?  Plus, the state has a lot of natural wonders that make it quite impressive.  Maybe not as many as Michigan, but still enough that it is worth going there.  We just got back from Texas with @mrsbozz's sister and brother in law, and we have already started throwing out ideas for our next city to visit.  Milwaukee was in the list of places to check out some day.  During our trip, we stuck mostly to the northern parts of the state, where the western shoreline of Lake Superior is absolutely amazing.


<center>![PXL_20260709_161910331.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23yTUjrZCeJjccRoUrGwbP8rAHasxdy94aoCiofTLMtzVxRypq7B2Xo47buHgArwB99y3.jpg)</center>

----------------------------------

If you ever get the chance to visit there, I highly recommend it!  The water is so pristine, the fish is amazing, and it is just a magical place.  I definitely want to take the time to explore more of the state if I ever get the chance.  I've heard the Dells area is pretty cool if not a bit touristy, and kind of commercialized now. 

Believe it or not, this is actually the penultimate episode of my #threetunetuesday series that is covering the fifty states of the United States.  We started all the way back at A with Alabama, and now here we are just about a year later rolling our way into Wisconsin before we move along to Wyoming to wrap things up.  In case you forgot, each of the three songs I am going to share needs to have Wisconsin in the title or lyrics.  It might have been easier if I could just reference a town in the state, but nope, I decided it needs to be the actual state name.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/5QRicsY5hOk?si=fEpFzmL3xXS21Uwn" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

----------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5QRicsY5hOk&list=RD5QRicsY5hOk&start_radio=1)

----------------------------

Believe it or not, Wisconsin was a lot harder than I thought it was going to be for this post.  Somehow in the back of my head, I thought there were a lot more songs that either mentioned Wisconsin or had it in the title, but I was very wrong.  I honestly struggled a bit to find the songs that I am going to share today.  Nancy Griffith is actually a pretty cool artist and she can write some really insightful lyrics.  I can appreciate that not everyone might like her style, or the twang of her voice, but if you don't like this song, at least dig into some of her slower stuff.  "Pearl's Eye View" is a new song for me, but it does have a reference to Wisconsin in it, so I figured I would share it here.  Plus, I am pretty sure I have never shared any of Griffith's songs before, so I thought that might be a cool thing to do as well.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/7T0nYP6ukSg?si=qWPxL_OAQEYAK5FH" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

--------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7T0nYP6ukSg&list=RD7T0nYP6ukSg&start_radio=1)

-------------------------

I've mentioned it before, but I always seem to get Tom Waits and John Waite messed up.  I know anyone who knows both artists probably thinks I am an idiot for that, but that's just how it is.  Sorry.  Anyway, in a pretty big departure from the kind of music you might be used to him playing, "Diamonds on My Windshield" is a kind of jazzy tune that is spoken more than it is sang.  Kind of in the vein of George Thorogoood or something like that.  If you listen closely, it does mention Wisconsin, so it fits the bill for this post.  Oddly enough, it seems like so far both of the videos I have shared today were from about 11 years ago.  I can promise you the last one will be a bit newer.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/ZZJxWqmP4Yw?si=E8I1sERn9qGDFm86" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>


---------------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZZJxWqmP4Yw&list=RDZZJxWqmP4Yw&start_radio=1)

--------------------------------

For this last one, I decided to go a totally different direction and give you "Wisconsin Death Trip" by Static X. I'll be the first to admit, I haven't listened to a lot of Static X in my lifetime, but it felt like a good idea to include it here.  If nothing else, I would like to think that these posts over the past year have kept you on your toes.  I like to sometimes throw in a little bit of the unexpected.  I feel this song fits really well with that.  These are all so different, that I wouldn't expect you to be able to pick any of them as your favorite, but I hope you at least enjoyed the variety!

Liebe Leser und Freunde des guten Films,

kürzlich (genau am 18.Okt.2026) wäre Klaus Kinski 100 Jahre alt geworden. Er war sicher einer der polarisierendsten deutschen Schauspieler überhaupt. Einerseits hatte er ohne Zweifel ein großes Talent gepaart mit dem Willen zu Perfektion, nicht umsonst hat ihn die Regie-Legende [Werner Herzog](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_Herzog) für mehrere Filmprojekte ausgewählt. Andererseits hatte er einen extrem aufbrausenden Charakter, wenn etwas nicht ganz in seinem Sinne verlief (was oft der Fall war).

Geboren wurde er wie gesagt 1926 in der Nähe von Danzig, in Pommern. Als er vier Jahre alt war, zog die Familie nach Berlin, wo er auch das Gymnasium absolvierte. Kurz vor Kriegsende wurde er eingezogen und geriet bei Arnheim im Dez. 1944 in brit. Kriegsgefangenschaft. In einem brit. Gefangenenlager in Essex spielte er auch seine ersten Theaterrollen.
1946 entlassen, kehrte er zurück nach Berlin und arbeitete als Schauspieler in Theatern und hatte 1947 seine erste Filmrolle. Schon früh neigte er zu Wutanfällen und wurde z.B. vom Berliner Schlosspark-Theater entlassen, nachdem er eine Scheibe zertrümmert hatte.
Ab 1952 versuchte er sich auch als Rezitator und trat in Berlin, München und Wien auf, in München wohnte er zeitweise in der gleichen Pension wie der noch junge Werner Herzog. Bekannter wurde er in den 1960ern durch Auftritte bei einigen [Edgar-Wallace-Filmen](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar-Wallace-Filme), wo er oft "zwielichtige oder psychisch auffällige" Figuren verkörperte. Auch hatte er eine Rolle in [Doktor Schiwago](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doktor_Schiwago_(1965)) (1965) und in einigen "[Spaghetti-Western](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italowestern)" (teilweise von Sergio Leone inszeniert und mit Clint Eastwood).

Legendär war sein Auftritt 1971 bei einer Lesung seines eigenen Werks "Jesus Christus Erlöser", die schon früh gestört wurde durch Zwischenrufe aus dem Publikum. Als ein Zuschauer meinte, Jesus sei duldsam gewesen und habe bei Widerspruch nicht „Halt deine Schnauze!“ gerufen, antwortete Kinski: „Nein, er hat nicht gesagt ‚Halt die Schnauze‘. Er hat eine Peitsche genommen und hat ihm in die Fresse gehauen! Das hat der gemacht. Du dumme Sau!“ So etwas ist heute überhaupt nicht mehr vorstellbar, aber damals passierte es wirklich.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jr2zPqoVs3A

Seine markanten Schurkenauftritte veranlassten vermutlich Werner Herzog, Kinski 1971 die Hauptrolle für seinen Film "Aguirre, der Zorn Gottes" anzubieten. Nach anfänglichem Zögern stimmte Kinski aufgrund seiner finanzieller Probleme zu. Kinski und Herzog drehten insgesamt noch vier andere Filme zusammen: "Nosferatu – Phantom der Nacht" (1978), "Woyzeck" (1979), "Fitzcarraldo" (1981) und "Cobra Verde" (1987). Alle 5 gelten als Meisterwerke!
Die Zusammenarbeit war zwar sehr fruchtbar, aber auch anstrengend wegen der regelmäßigen Tobsuchtsanfällen Kinskis, z.B. hier bei den schwierigen Dreharbeiten für Fitzcarraldo im peruanischen Dschungel (auch die Kommentare unter dem folgenden Video sind lesenswert😃).
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-n2kcLAYQBs

Werner Herzog hatte später eine interessante Reportage ("Mein liebster Feind", 1999) gedreht, in der er seine komplexe Hassliebe zu Kinski beschrieb:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oPiVyDq8EKo
Bemerkenswert an dem Video sind für mich 2 Dinge, erstens, dass Herzog meinte, Kinski sei der einzige Mensch gewesen, von dem er etwas lernen konnte, und zweitens, dass sie oft nur kurz nach seinen Wutausbrüchen gedreht hatten, auf Drängen Herzogs, und dass Kinski immer dann besonders eindrucksvoll, "wie sonst niemand auf der Welt" war. Diese negative Energie bzw. diese Aggression, die Kinski in sich trug, war also durchaus produktiv und Herzog wusste sie zu nutzen, vielleicht war das das Erfolgsgeheimnis dieses so ungleichen Duos.

1989 schuf Kinski mit "Kinski Paganini" sein letztes Filmwerk. Er hatte Regie, Drehbuch, Schnitt und die Hauptrolle selbst übernommen, da er den Stoff vergeblich Produzenten und Regisseuren angetragen hatte; auch Werner Herzog hatte das Drehbuch für unverfilmbar gehalten. Der Film wurde von den Kritikern zerrissen. Es sollte seine einzige Regiearbeit und sein letzter Film bleiben - am  23. Nov. 1991 starb er mit 65 in Kalifornien (er hatte dort ein Haus) an einem Herzinfarkt.

Klaus Kinski war wie kaum ein andere Mensch ein Beispiel dafür, wie eng Genie und Wahnsinn beieinanderliegen.

Wer kannte Kinski noch bzw. wer hat Filme von ihm gesehen? Für mich war am eindrucksvollsten Fitzcarraldo.
Dort spielt er einen Opern-Enthusiasten, der im Dschungel ein Opernhaus bauen will und dafür das scheinbar Unmögliche versucht.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23wMYTAiM1QJQc8xfq9umWn32m3bdeKg8rvP2Uy1JaL41bfKJhHHN56EF9Gn3NqrubbWm.png)

Genial auch seine Verkörperung von Graf Dracula in "Nosferatu".
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23vsBnZrtkL5fvf35nzfuSSiiC32QayR7Py6AUBqCFkJ4ZKYSP7PkJdkopExX75Ue6hDK.png)

-------------------------------

I'm running on fumes this morning. Last week my wife and I cut out of work early on Thursday and started our long weekend to celebrate a few things.  Way back in the Spring, my sister and law as well as myself turned 50 about a month apart from each other.  At the time, she didn't really want to do anything special for it, but eventually she changed her mind.  So the four of us (spouses included) started to brainstorm where we might travel to as a celebration.  

This past weekend worked out perfect for all of us due to the fact that their school district where my sister in law and her husband work, as well as our school district where @mrsbozz and I both work had Friday off.  So a few text exchanges later, and we had plans set to visit Austin, Texas.

This also just happened to fall on the weekend of @mrsbozz and I's 18th anniversary, so it was kind of a double celebration.


<center>![PXL_20261018_232625570.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EoiUjX68z7e1YbsTRYrAoZSY9JvfxRVFAHbhU4TRJodfSGQgdwvmsbdYdGtH3EzMnMw.jpg)</center>

--------------------------

We spent about 10 hours traveling yesterday between the air and the land, an I am just about as dead as can be.  I actually feel like I am a bit outside of my body right now.  I think it is a combination of the slight time change, being tired in general, and probably being a bit dehydrated to boot.  Needless to say, I am just "off".  It's going to be a long road for me catching up on this Monday, between my real job and HIVE which I have been neglecting for the past three days.

After I publish this post, I will be working on comments, then I will be catching up on the posts I missed from the weekend.  It's like a second job sometimes!  

Needless to say, this post is going to be pretty short, but trust me, I have some cool stuff for you in the future.  We packed so much into the last three days, and it didn't really even begin to scratch the surface of everything Austin has to offer.


<center>![PXL_20261016_014452887.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23swnH6aGNTtQwnNovCFSMa4RfLWwjZLMeSpk8D8fbAU5g5qyh9gEomxFD5SqshoWv3Ts.jpg)</center>

----------------------------

One thing I am beginning to realize is just how important booking a "recovery day" from traveling is.  As my wife and I get older, this is really starting to become apparent.  It would have been really nice today to be able to just relax at home, get caught up on laundry, and just kind of decompress from all the excitement of the past weekend.  You know how people say "I need a vacation from my vacation"?  That's exactly how this feels.  

Anyway, trust me when I say, if you forgive my laziness today, but stick with me through the next couple of weeks, you will see some pretty awesome food and hear about some really amazing experiences that we had on our trip.  Probably not until Wednesday though.  Tomorrow will be a music post since it is Tuesday and we only have two more states to get through for my musical road trip across the US.

I'm in tremendous amount of pain. I'm seeing a lot of people surrounding me losing it. Some taken away by illness, some rendered in total disablement, some are critical condition, but I will leave that part later in the end of this story. For now, I'd like to use this drawing to express my feelings towards the current economy.


# 1. The nose dive
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXbYF7UafCU5gLyBGBuJs392zGjn9qcoHYEupaqY5MUfh/1792424840049.jpg)
I was trying to find inspiration everywhere, but mostly about penguins, ostrich, paper plane with a cncrete slab... I couldn't make up my mind. I do have preference on twin verticle stabilizers, especially the Malaysian MIG29.

# 2. Fuel guzzlers
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPKViuXLKP8NPDs1zMsgNgRHyrHdcfH8myMmA4uyJMnEu/1792424840132.jpg)
Fighter pilot YouTuber  #gonkey was once an instructor for the RMAF described, it was a unique experience to see a MIG29 emitting black smoke not far from a F18 sharing the same taxi way. Stating that MIG29 was a heavy black smoker. MIG29 the older generation fighter jet is also known for its high fuel consumption.

# 3. Retired for good
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmakYeFHjYJHDX4tSK5e9Bzn48iQqGGf2ubYVpcvYA9BEd/1792424840194.jpg)
I'm looping a long ribbon on one of the vertical stabilizer and tied it with a balloon. With such high fuel demanding machine, a young country like Malaysia, I'm not surprised the Royal air force no longer able to keep them flying anymore, unless these jets runs on helium.

# 4. Like it or not
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPfiDx4XPdCh7G4YDXyhnDBzi4R8q7BoSb5NvPJaNkrV5/1792424840256.jpg)
Technically, I'm not really street smart on "perspective". The curvature of the balloon has to be gridded before I can finish it up with wording and shadings. These jets are old. There's no way we can keep burning kerosene for acrobatics show during independence day. With the war going on, pressure on fuel price is also driving every one nuts. No one single engined vehicle are depending on helium. Funny enough, the other day when I fuel up my car, the the waterboy holding a helium balloon, and it has a label of RON95.

# 5. It hurt
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU56aHpf1iDrHytPK6wCmvEdeKNzYCyriNS28DXoBv3Dv/1792424840312.jpg)
Whilst the fighter jet has absolutely nothing related to my living lifestyle. But the fuel price caused by the war, already spun up a serious inflation. I'm using a fighter jet as an object, it can be a car, it can be anything under the influence of fuel price that resulting in anything "flightless" operating cost keep getting higher and higher, and we can't do absofuckinglutely nothing about it.

Recently I found a long lost friend from the newspaper headline, that he was found dead "fell" from the building. Nobody wanna use the S word, as that may affect any insurance claim proceeding. I just can't imagine what is going through his mind. I wish he could have at least considered himself flightless before commiting it. I'm still feeling tremendous amount of pain, and sometimes I even dream of felling off and woke up from an intense "stepping into a void" situation.

![Cottage.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR9RB9NKvZ2yCtxRN1RnSXtWiMQFUA3vCHxNQMXZt7DUQ/Cottage.png)
The long winter up here makes summer premium outdoor activity. So much so that I refuse to stop adventuring summer style well into the fall. In this tale, I am challenging myself to share an immersive autumn cottage getaway to cottage wilderness through only 8 photos!
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
# The Cottage
![IMG_0266.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZj82aNHWbPB8E3EaWgfQmXMJvEJ1qMSAtnENNhwbq3KJ/IMG_0266.jpg)
You know when you find yourself lucky enough to have a privilege that really shouldn't be afforded to you? Not that you don't deserve it but you have not earned it from the results of your decisions. The cottage I get to visit regularly is that to me and I am challenged to share our latest trip in 8 picture or less.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0252 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQz1wPrexJqsmXAARaNVpR31XMYTvQctxME3J2BWyHknn/IMG_0252%20(1).jpg)
After the long drive, I make it a point to walk right to the deck and look over the lake that feeds itself right to our toes. I can feel the wieght of it as I breathe in the clean air and shed the mantle of regular schedule and duty.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0255 (2).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPmAJaUFYow4Hfpzm3LocB3h52g8GWHVK8xzwzQcf1y4a/IMG_0255%20(2).jpg)
After we settle in and enjoy a meal, I pillage the wood pile and build a fire to warm and entertain in the cool autumn night. No televisions, no plans to hit the town, just a couple pints beside the fire to make my clothes smell like campfire as the stars brighten in the clear darkening sky.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0258 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVkbL9kSAgWWMotWV85G2UEFg5sVzR7TLgf3gZnpTEWn5/IMG_0258%20(1).jpg)
Speaking of beers, a card-carrying beerologist wouldn't think to visit the cottage without a few pints! If you would like to delve deeper into the local craft beer adventure up in this particular region of cottage country, feel free to visit [HERE!](https://new.hive.blog/beersaturday/@zekepickleman/beersaturday-more-cottage-beers) I just love visiting the my favourite of the craft breweries in the area and fuel up for a couple days lakeside.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0256 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXyran4gkXdHZij2ZChsxBaSLXCQ4LTiYdmtsoM4vSWvG/IMG_0256%20(1).jpg)
October brings Canadian Thanksgiving over a month before the much larger spectacle holiday to the south in the USA. Scattered warm and sunny days encourage us that summer is not waning so fast and then the cool nights remind us winter is on the way. The forecast showed relatively mild daytime highs but promised a little cool rain as well. Happy to put on a layer and enjoy watching the sun try and break through the clouds over the lake. Quiet this time of year as many have losed their cottages for the year.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0262 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcePfxf4DP3JNzmJJrpRNq1YPHChn5ThKMJyANUWsQN4C/IMG_0262%20(1).jpg)
Thew fall is just as perfect for a paddle on the lake. We took the boat out to travel around the bend to a neighbouring camp fire and out to the dock for a cold final swim of the year. The colours are thrilling and the mallards seem to be delaying their migration south.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0277.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbtopmFkqWwcuarsUqjPqWv3FeJoyNojw3ahqQhYqfBUN/IMG_0277.jpg)
Sitting on the edge of the lake toward the end of our short stay in one of our happy places, it is so nice to be close to wild life. The mallards happily tip down to feast on the late season weeds. Blue Jays swoop down to snap up some of the peanuts we leave on the rails. We can hear the loons call over the lake like in some classic Canadian commercial.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0279 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbhZWUTHWphNPhA47xHwBj2QUCw8UWLxrfqC2wEsqGC2M/IMG_0279%20(1).jpg)
After a refreshing weekend of relaxation, family feast, out door lounging and that last cold plunge of the season, I look back at the cottage. With all the preparations made to close it down for the year, it will sit peacevully as the snow piles up and nature takes it back for a season. Happy for the time spent, hopeful for some more next year, and grateful for the opportunity to return here to celebrate an escape with family.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0280.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWrmDeP6zsnWqx49yYbMNyvjwoTabGs3ZzFihH9RTx2Qq/IMG_0280.jpg)
A few extra moments lingering at the edge of the lake, drinking in the clean air while surrounded by fantastic colours.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
![IMG_0281.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXaAc3tWafRtRBd6duJXrg9YKiTFzTQPP5FUQd6nZVVzn/IMG_0281.jpg)
One last picture from my happy place to share with the world. I am sure there are wonderful places like this all around the world. While many will never get to visit Canada, I am happy for those who will have the opportunity. I hope they find a place like this and discover a few reasons I love being here so much. # Thank you for joining me for one last weekend before winter!
![image (9).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zekepickleman/23zufAZhV9dt6F5XnFS8u5zdRtARKHnwZT4CZECiscnUBWMzc2vsH7vZuFSXcNNuyGDo5.png)
